pain_title: Assessment should not require five disconnected tools.
pain_intro: Every hand-off creates more administration and less time for teaching.
solution_intro: EzProctor brings authoring, delivery, monitoring, coding and grading together.
solution_points: Review one answer book per student

pain_title: Why should coding students leave the exam to test their code?
pain_intro: External IDEs break the assessment flow and reduce educator visibility.
solution_intro: The practical coding IDE stays inside the secure exam experience.

pain_title: The exam ends. The marking workload begins.
pain_intro: Large answer volumes make consistent review difficult and slow.
solution_intro: Advisory pre-grading supports educators without replacing their judgement.

pain_title: A lost answer should never decide a student's result.
pain_intro: Browser crashes and network interruptions create avoidable assessment risk.
pain_points: Manual save is easy to forget
solution_title: Keep the latest official student work.
solution_intro: EzProctor synchronises answer progress to the assessment database.

pain_title: Rebuilding every question by hand is not assessment design.
pain_intro: Educators already have question papers. The platform should respect that work.
solution_intro: Bring existing papers into a structured exam workflow.

pain_title: Who has started? Who is active? Who has submitted?
pain_intro: During an exam, educators need answers at a glance, not another spreadsheet.
solution_title: A live operational view for every session.
solution_intro: Simple visual status keeps the educator focused on the room.

pain_title: One assessment can include more than one kind of thinking.
pain_intro: Written explanations and practical code should belong in the same exam.
solution_intro: Use the right answer experience for each question type.

pain_title: Exam-day setup should not become the first question.
pain_intro: Complex workstation preparation increases support pressure before students begin.
solution_intro: The EzProctor desktop client connects students to the exam on the local network.

pain_title: Assessment evidence should be ready when audit day arrives.
pain_intro: Reconstructing student work after the session is slow and risky.
pain_points: Code and written work are separated
solution_title: One complete answer book per student.
solution_intro: Create a consistent record across every question in the exam.
solution_points: PDF export for review and backup

pain_title: AI advice should not become an automatic final grade.
pain_intro: Assessment decisions need context, accountability and educator judgement.
solution_title: AI can advise. The educator decides.
solution_intro: Model answers support pre-grading while confirmation remains human-led.

pain_title: Students should spend exam time answering, not navigating.
pain_intro: Long status lists and unclear progress create unnecessary cognitive load.
pain_points: Answered items are hard to review
solution_intro: Visual question status helps students move confidently through the exam.

pain_title: A practical exam should not depend on the public internet.
pain_intro: Connectivity uncertainty can turn assessment delivery into incident management.
solution_title: Run the assessment on your own network.

pain_intro: Educators and IT teams need visibility into the platform they depend on.
solution_intro: Inspect, implement and contribute to the EzProctor project.

pain_title: Marks alone do not help students understand their learning.
pain_intro: Useful feedback is often delayed by the volume of assessment administration.
solution_title: Review evidence, feedback and marks together.
solution_intro: A question-focused grading workspace supports consistent educator decisions.
